metaTitle: SIR30216 Cert III in Retail RPL — Fast Track & Online
metaDescription: Working in retail? Get the SIR30216 Certificate III in Retail through RPL using your shop floor experience. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SIR30216 Certificate III in Retail is the core qualification for experienced retail staff. If you already serve customers, make sales and work in a retail team, RPL lets you get it using evidence from your job.
whoIsItFor:
• Retail assistants and sales associates
  • Senior sales staff and key holders
  • Visual merchandisers and stock staff with customer service duties
  • Supermarket and department store team members

Candidates usually have six months or more in retail: engaging customers, selling, handling customer difficulties, building loyalty, teamwork, store security and WHS.
evidenceExamples:
• Sales results or KPI reports
  • Customer feedback or mystery shopper results
  • Training records from your employer, such as product, POS or loss prevention training
  • Rosters showing your role and hours
  • A reference from your store manager
description:
The SIR30216 Certificate III in Retail covers the skills of experienced retail staff: engaging customers, selling, building customer relationships and loyalty, assisting with customer difficulties, working in a team and a service environment, responding to security risks and contributing to WHS.

Electives cover areas such as visual merchandising, stock control and online retail. The next step is the SIR40316 Certificate IV in Retail Management.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate III in Retail through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you work in retail. Your sales results, customer feedback, training records and a manager's reference are assessed against the units.
Usually 4 to 8 weeks.
Mostly. Evidence is submitted online, and your manager confirms your skills in the store.

faqs.q: I'm a store supervisor. Which qualification suits me?
faqs.a: If you lead a team or run the store, the Certificate IV in Retail Management is usually a better fit.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Ask for a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: SIR40316 Cert IV Retail Management RPL — Online
metaDescription: Store manager or supervisor? Get the SIR40316 Certificate IV in Retail Management through RPL using your experience. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SIR40316 Certificate IV in Retail Management is the qualification for store managers and retail supervisors. If you already lead a team, manage store financials and drive sales, RPL lets you get it using evidence from your role.
whoIsItFor:
• Store managers and assistant store managers
  • Retail supervisors and team leaders
  • Department managers in large stores
  • Retail business owners

Candidates usually have a year or more leading a retail team: rosters, sales targets, store financials, staff relations, store security and WHS.

Entry requirements: you need the SIR30216 Certificate III in Retail, or relevant retail work experience using the skills of its core units. Most retail supervisors meet this through their work history.
evidenceExamples:
• Sales and KPI reports for your store or team
  • Rosters, wage budgets and store P&L reports
  • Team meeting notes, coaching and performance records (with names removed)
  • Store security and WHS records
  • A reference from your area or regional manager
description: The SIR40316 Certificate IV in Retail Management covers leading a retail store or team: monitoring store financials, creating a customer-centric culture, maintaining employee relations, leading a frontline team, maintaining store security, achieving sales results and maintaining workplace safety.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate IV in Retail Management through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you lead a retail team or store. Your sales reports, rosters, financials and a reference from your area manager are assessed against the units.

faqs.q: Do I need the Certificate III in Retail first?
faqs.a: Not if you have relevant retail work experience. That experience meets the entry requirement.
Usually 4 to 8 weeks.
Mostly. Evidence is submitted online, and your manager confirms your skills.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Ask for a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: SIT20125 Cert II in Tourism RPL — Fast Track
metaDescription: Working in tourism? Get the SIT20125 Certificate II in Tourism through RPL using your customer service experience. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SIT20125 Certificate II in Tourism is the entry-level tourism qualification. If you already work with visitors, for example at a visitor centre, attraction or tour company, RPL lets you get it using evidence from your job.
whoIsItFor:
• Visitor information and front desk staff
  • Attraction, theme park and museum staff
  • Tour desk and booking assistants
  • Tourism workers early in their career

Candidates usually have six months or more in a tourism role: giving customers information and help, using knowledge of the tourism industry, showing cultural sensitivity and working safely.
evidenceExamples:
• A reference from your supervisor describing your role
  • Customer feedback or reviews that mention you
  • Training records from your employer
  • Rosters or a statement of service
  • Examples of information or bookings you've handled (with customer details removed)
description:
The SIT20125 Certificate II in Tourism covers the foundations of working in tourism: sourcing and using tourism industry information, providing customer information and help, interacting with customers, showing social and cultural sensitivity and working safely.

It replaces SIT20122 and SIT20116.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate II in Tourism through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you work with visitors in a tourism role. A supervisor's reference, customer feedback and training records are assessed against the units.
Usually 3 to 6 weeks.

faqs.q: What comes after the Certificate II?
faqs.a: Many people move on to the Certificate IV in Travel and Tourism once they take on more responsibility.
Mostly. Evidence is submitted online, and your supervisor confirms your skills.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Ask for a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: SIT30222 Cert III in Travel RPL — Travel Consultant
metaDescription: Working as a travel consultant? Get the SIT30222 Certificate III in Travel through RPL using your agency experience. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SIT30222 Certificate III in Travel is the qualification for travel consultants. If you already advise customers, build itineraries, quote and book travel, RPL lets you get it using evidence from your work.
whoIsItFor:
• Retail and corporate travel consultants
  • Reservations and ticketing staff
  • Online and home-based travel agents
  • Travel consultants who trained overseas

Candidates usually have a year or more as a travel consultant: advising on Australian and international destinations, preparing quotes, constructing international airfares, using a reservations system and processing bookings.
evidenceExamples:
• Itineraries and quotes you've prepared (with customer details removed)
  • Booking records from your GDS or reservations system
  • Airfare and ticketing work you've completed
  • Product and destination training certificates
  • A reference from your agency manager
licensingInfo: There's no state licence for travel agents in Australia. Many agencies belong to the industry accreditation scheme (ATAS), and employers often look for a recognised qualification.
description:
The SIT30222 Certificate III in Travel covers the work of a travel consultant: sourcing tourism and product information, advising on international and Australian destinations, selling tourism products, preparing quotations, booking products and processing documentation, using a computerised reservations system, constructing international airfares, customer service and cultural sensitivity.

It replaces SIT30216.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate III in Travel through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you work as a travel consultant. Your itineraries, quotes, booking records and an agency reference are assessed against the units.

faqs.q: Do I need a licence to be a travel agent?
faqs.a: No, there's no state licence in Australia. Employers and the industry accreditation scheme often look for a recognised qualification like this one.
Usually 4 to 8 weeks.
Yes, 100% online from anywhere in Australia.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Ask for a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: SIT40125 Cert IV Travel & Tourism RPL — Fast Track
metaDescription: Senior travel or tourism professional? Get the SIT40125 Certificate IV in Travel and Tourism through RPL. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SIT40125 Certificate IV in Travel and Tourism is the qualification for senior travel and tourism staff and supervisors. If you already lead customer experiences, coach others and handle financial information, RPL lets you get it using evidence from your role.
whoIsItFor:
• Senior travel consultants and team leaders
  • Tour coordinators and senior tour guides
  • Tourism supervisors at attractions, visitor centres and operators
  • Tourism business owners

Candidates usually have a few years in travel or tourism, including improving customer experiences, managing conflict, interpreting financial information and coaching staff.
evidenceExamples:
• Itineraries, tours or packages you've designed or run
  • Customer feedback and service improvements you've led
  • Sales or financial reports you work with
  • Training or coaching you've given staff
  • A reference from your manager or business partner
description:
The SIT40125 Certificate IV in Travel and Tourism covers senior and supervisory work: sourcing tourism industry information, enhancing customer service experiences, managing conflict, interpreting financial information, coaching others, cultural sensitivity and WHS.

Electives cover areas such as tour coordination, guiding, product development, sales and travel consulting. It replaces SIT40122 and SIT40116.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate IV in Travel and Tourism through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you work in a senior travel or tourism role. Your itineraries or tours, customer feedback, financial reports and a reference are assessed against the units.
Usually 4 to 8 weeks.
Mostly. Evidence is submitted online, and your workplace confirms your skills.

faqs.q: What's the next step after this?
faqs.a: Managers usually move on to the Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Ask for a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: SIT50122 Diploma of Travel & Tourism Management RPL
metaDescription: Manage a travel or tourism business? Get the SIT50122 Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management through RPL. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SIT50122 Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management is the management qualification for travel and tourism. If you already manage a team, budget and customer service in an agency, tour operator or attraction, RPL lets you get it using evidence from your role.
whoIsItFor:
• Travel agency managers
  • Tour operations and product managers
  • Attraction, visitor centre and tourism business managers
  • Tourism business owners

Candidates usually have several years in travel or tourism, with a management role covering people, budgets, customer service quality, business relationships and online reputation.
evidenceExamples:
• Budgets and financial reports you manage
  • Customer service standards and quality systems
  • Supplier and partner agreements
  • Staff management and rostering records
  • Online reputation and review management
  • A reference from the owner or senior manager
description:
The SIT50122 Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management covers managing a travel or tourism business: leading diversity and inclusion, managing online reputation risk, developing quality customer service, managing finances and budgets, leading people, monitoring operations, building business relationships, managing conflict and WHS.

It replaces SIT50116.
searchAliases: diploma of travel and tourism management rpl

faqs.q: Can I get the Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you manage in travel or tourism. Your budgets, service standards, staff records and a senior reference are assessed against the units.
Usually 6 to 10 weeks.
Mostly. Evidence is submitted online, and your workplace confirms your management skills.

faqs.q: Do I need the Certificate IV first?
faqs.a: No, there are no entry requirements. Management experience in travel or tourism is what matters.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Ask for a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: SIT60122 Adv Diploma Travel & Tourism Management RPL
metaDescription: Manage a travel or tourism business? Get the SIT60122 Advanced Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management through RPL. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SIT60122 Advanced Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management is the senior management qualification for travel and tourism. If you already manage a travel agency, tour company or tourism business, RPL lets you get it using evidence from your work.
whoIsItFor:
• Travel agency and branch managers
  • Tour operators and tourism business owners
  • Tourism product and operations managers
  • Destination and visitor centre managers

Candidates usually have several years managing in travel or tourism: business planning, budgets and financial reports, product development, marketing, legal compliance and leading staff.
evidenceExamples:
• Business and marketing plans
  • Budgets and financial reports
  • Tourism products or packages you developed
  • Policies, risk and WHS documents
  • A reference from the owner, board or general manager
description:
The SIT60122 Advanced Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management covers senior management in travel and tourism. Its 17 core units include business planning and risk, interpreting financial information and managing budgets, developing tourism products, quality customer service, legal compliance, marketing strategy, leading people and diversity, and WHS systems, plus ten electives.

It replaces SIT60116 and sits above the SIT50122 Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management.
searchAliases: advanced diploma of travel and tourism management

faqs.q: Can I get the Advanced Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you manage in travel or tourism. Your business plans, financial reports, products and a reference are assessed against the units.

faqs.q: Should I choose the Diploma or the Advanced Diploma?
faqs.a: The Diploma suits managers of a team or department. The Advanced Diploma is for people running the whole business, including its plans, finances and strategy.
Usually 6 to 10 weeks.
Yes. Evidence is submitted online, and your workplace confirms your skills.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.
